No family history of Parkinson's disease

social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 15 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait instability with freezing, urinary accidents, and forgetfulness over 18 months
patient.history_present_illness: A 71-year-old retired factory supervisor with hypertension and well-controlled type 2 diabetes was admitted for evaluation of progressive gait instability, urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline over the past 18 months. His wife first noticed he was walking more slowly and with a shuffle about 18 months ago. She thought he looked 'like an old man all of a sudden.' Over the following months he began to freeze when approaching doorways and narrow spaces, and he has had three falls — twice at home and once in a parking lot. He was previously a confident and active man who enjoyed weekend gardening; he now needs help getting up from low chairs and avoids stairs when possible. His wife notes that he has become noticeably forgetful — he forgets conversations from the day before, has difficulty following the news, and becomes frustrated when he cannot recall words. He denies resting tremor, and his wife confirms she has not seen a tremor. Urinary urgency began approximately 12 months ago and has progressed to frank incontinence with two to three accidents per week. His internist evaluated him and obtained a head CT showing markedly enlarged ventricles. He was referred for neurology workup and admitted for MRI, lumbar puncture, and tap trial. He is nervous about the lumbar puncture but cooperative.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. MoCA 22/30. Deficits in delayed recall (2/5), abstraction, and executive function (clock drawing clock face intact but hands incorrect). No aphasia. Normal insight.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. Vertical gaze full.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone. No rigidity. No resting tremor. No bradykinesia. Strength full bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild vibration loss at bilateral great toes. Light touch and proprioception intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based magnetic shuffling gait. Short steps, reduced arm swing bilaterally. Freezing at doorway. TUG 25 seconds. 10-meter walk 19 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test positive — 2 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Positive grasp reflex bilaterally. No nuchal rigidity.

findings.location: bilateral lateral ventricles and third ventricle
sulci at high convexity vs Sylvian fissures

mri.impression: Classic iNPH findings: Evans index 0.37, callosal angle 76°, DESH pattern with disproportionate high-convexity sulcal effacement, transependymal periventricular signal, and prominent aqueductal flow void. Mild background white matter disease. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 44 mg/dL. Glucose: 74 mg/dL (ratio 0.65). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 742 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 208 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 24 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with TUG and 10-meter walk

findings.freezing: Doorway freezing not observed at 24-hour reassessment

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 32% at 24 hours (25 sec to 17 sec); 10-meter walk improved 32% (19 sec to 13 sec); MoCA improved 2 points (22 to 24). Doorway freezing was not observed at 24-hour reassessment. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 14, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

Hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF flow. Peak velocity 21 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 76 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — uninhibited contractions at 140 mL. Maximum capacity 240 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Uninhibited contractions at 140 mL; maximum cystometric capacity 240 mL. No outlet obstruction identified. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Pre-tap moderately impaired; post-tap mildly impaired — significant improvement
Pre-tap moderately impaired; post-tap improvement to mildly impaired
Pre-tap mildly impaired; post-tap marginal improvement

output.impression: Post-tap improvement in frontal-subcortical cognitive domains. Executive function improved from moderately to mildly impaired; processing speed improved from moderately to mildly impaired. Memory showed marginal improvement. The pattern of improvement is most pronounced in executive function and processing speed. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Normal bilateral striatal dopamine transporter uptake — symmetric, no putaminal loss

output.impression: Normal striatal dopamine transporter uptake. Bilateral symmetric uptake in caudate and putamen without reduction. No evidence of presynaptic dopaminergic deficit. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: NPH differentiation from Parkinson's disease DaTscan magnetic gait

results.title: DaTscan in differentiating NPH from Parkinson's disease
results.key_finding: Normal DaTscan effectively excludes Parkinson's disease; NPH gait is wide-based magnetic vs parkinsonian narrow-based festinant. Both may show reduced arm swing.

results.title: Gait characteristics in iNPH vs Parkinson's disease
results.key_finding: NPH gait is wide-based magnetic; PD gait is narrow-based festinant. Step height distinction is key.

output.summary: Normal DaTscan findings effectively exclude presynaptic dopaminergic neurodegeneration. Wide-based magnetic gait with freezing, in the absence of tremor, differs from the narrow-based festinant pattern of Parkinson's disease. Tap trial TUG improvement >20% is associated with VP shunt response in iNPH.

critical_actions: Confirm normal CSF opening pressure (≤18 cmH2O)
Quantify TUG improvement at 24 hours post-tap (>20% required)
Exclude Parkinson's disease clinically (no tremor, no rigidity, normal DaTscan)
Prompt neurosurgery referral — VP shunt with programmable valve
contraindicated_actions: Empirical trial of levodopa without DaTscan — delays correct diagnosis
Attributing gait disorder to diabetic neuropathy without NPH workup
Deferring tap trial because of patient anxiety — counsel and proceed
key_reasoning_points: Classic Hakim's triad over 18 months in a 71-year-old man
Evans index 0.37, callosal angle 76°, DESH — clear iNPH imaging
Normal opening pressure (14 cmH2O) — meets required criterion
32% TUG improvement is a robust positive tap trial response
Normal DaTscan effectively excludes Parkinson's disease
Negative amyloid PET confirms iNPH-only pathology for excellent shunt prognosis

red_herrings.data_point: Family history of memory problems in father after age 75
red_herrings.intended_effect: Concern for familial Alzheimer's disease may delay NPH workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CSF biomarkers and amyloid PET are negative. Cognitive impairment is from NPH, not familial AD.

red_herrings.data_point: Reduced arm swing bilaterally with gait freezing — potential Parkinsonism
red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait features may be misinterpreted as parkinsonian, prompting levodopa trial instead of NPH workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Gait is wide-based magnetic (NPH), not narrow-based festinant (PD). No tremor or rigidity. Normal DaTscan confirms no nigrostriatal degeneration.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH in a 71-year-old retired factory supervisor — classic Hakim's triad, clear MRI, strongly positive tap trial. Parkinsonian gait features and family history of dementia as minor red herrings.
